The *Tīṇuppalamāliyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 375) is a verse biographical narrative preserved within the Therāpadāna, a late collection in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past karmic deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder (thera) associated with an offering of three water lilies (uppala) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. On SuttaCentral, five modern translations across five languages are recorded [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels and automated text-reuse analyses demonstrate close structural relationships within the Apadāna corpus. SuttaCentral identifies an earlier homonymous poem, Tha Ap 344 (*Tīṇuppalamāliyattheraapadāna*), as a full parallel [SuttaCentral]. This is corroborated by DharmaNexus computational analysis, which aligns almost the entirety of the text (§0.2–11.1) with Tha Ap 344 with very high similarity [DharmaNexus]. In total, DharmaNexus identifies 62 matching passages across 16 Pali texts, including extensive sharing of standard formulaic verses with commentarial sources like the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as numerous related botanical offering apadānas such as the *Dhajadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 345), *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 270, Tha Ap 372), and *Pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 374) [DharmaNexus]. Automatic cross-language alignment also records low-scoring matches with Tibetan Mahāyāna texts, including the *Candrottarādārikāvyākaraṇa-sūtra* (D 191) and *Samādhirāja-sūtra* (D 127), though these reflect stock phrases rather than genuine historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
